inputs.root_cause: SAL-ORA-OBL-EC8D65524EB96820 (ORA-EDIT-001) requires transactional add/replace/move/rename/remove operations for groups/layers/assets/metadata. Before this slice, apply_transaction was already fully generic (any OraImage -> OraImage callable built via dataclasses.replace() is a valid step), but only add and rename were exercised by any test; replace, move, and remove were never exercised, and neither were group targets.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 5 new tests in test_obligation_transactional_edit.py prove replace, move, and remove against both a layer target and a group target (OraStack nesting is the group mechanism), including a group removal that carries its children with it, plus a rollback proof combining a replace and a group-remove that both revert together on a later failure.

execution_steps: 1. Read transaction.py directly: apply_transaction takes arbitrary EditStep callables (OraImage -> OraImage), already fully generic -- not a per-operation API. Read the existing test file's _add_layer/_add_member/_rename_root helpers to confirm the established pattern: a step helper builds a new model tree via dataclasses.replace() and returns a new OraImage.
2. Read model/stack.py: OraStack nests OraStack/OraLayer/OraText children in visual order, confirming a 'group' is simply a non-root OraStack -- no separate group concept to build.

3. Wrote an interactive probe script constructing an image with a nested group and a sibling layer, then built and ran replace/move/remove step functions (including removing an entire group) directly against apply_transaction, confirming all 5 scenarios (replace, move-into-group, remove-layer, remove-group, and a combined-rollback case) worked correctly on the first attempt before writing any formal test.

4. Formalized the probe into 5 new pytest tests plus a new _image_with_group() fixture and 4 new step-helper functions (_replace_layer, _move_layer_into_group, _remove_layer, _remove_group), added OraStack to the test file's imports.

5. Ran ruff (clean) and the full ora suite (294 passed, was 289) before writing any evidence claim. Left the obligation status at 'partial' rather than promoting to 'implemented': metadata targets remain untested (no metadata concept exists anywhere in the model) and reference-maintenance/stale-derived-view-invalidation remain untested (no reference type or rendering engine exists) -- both real, substantive, unaddressed parts of the obligation's own MUST rule_text, not force-closed per this session's established discipline of not over-promoting partial obligations with genuinely unaddressed scope remaining.

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not cross-checked against a reference OpenRaster implementation.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: 0 obligations promoted to implemented; SAL-ORA-OBL-EC8D65524EB96820 stays partial with its scope honestly narrowed -- replace/move/remove/group-target coverage closed via 5 new tests against an already-generic mechanism, while metadata-target and reference/stale-view coverage remain genuinely open per GAP-008.
